root_cause.text: In `xchk_btree_check_block_owner()` in XFS scrub, the code dereferenced `bs->cur->bc_ops` after `bs->sc->sa.bno_cur` or `bs->sc->sa.rmap_cur` could already have been freed, causing a use-after-free when checking whether `bs->cur` aliases those pointers.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `xfs_btree_is_bno(bs->cur->bc_ops)` and `xfs_btree_is_rmap(bs->cur->bc_ops)` into early boolean samples (`is_bnobt`, `is_rmapbt`) “before any freeing could happen,” and then uses those cached values instead of dereferencing `bs->cur` in the later `if (!bs->sc->sa.bno_cur && ...)` / `if (!bs->sc->sa.rmap_cur && ...)` checks; the commit message explicitly says “We cannot dereference bs->cur when trying to determine if bs->cur aliases bs->sc->sa.{bno,rmap}_cur after the latter has been freed.”

intent_record.what: The function `xchk_btree_check_block_owner()` adds two local boolean variables, `is_bnobt` and `is_rmapbt`, and initializes them by calling `xfs_btree_is_bno(bs->cur->bc_ops)` and `xfs_btree_is_rmap(bs->cur->bc_ops)` immediately before computing `agno` and `agbno`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now records whether the current btree cursor is for the bnobt or rmapbt type, likely so later ownership-check logic can branch on those tree types and apply the correct block-owner validation rules.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use precomputed btree type flags instead of querying bs->cur->bc_ops directly when deciding whether to nullify the cursor.

intent_record.how: At runtime, the logic is unchanged in effect but now relies on precomputed btree-type flags instead of re-evaluating the btree operation predicates through bs->cur->bc_ops, which avoids depending on bs->cur in those conditions and makes the self-nullification path safer when bs->cur may be cleared.
